text:
alex_support: @maria_customer thanks for the report — can you confirm the Private control plane URL you're using? you mentioned TLS errors and DNS timeouts in your ticket.

maria_customer: Using https://control.redwood.internal:443. From our side we see `curl: (35) SSL connect error` and occasional `lookup control.redwood.internal: no such host`. Started after we tightened egress NP yesterday.

alex_support: Are you running Calico/Cilium/other? Any default-deny networkpolicy for egress?

maria_customer: Calico, yes. We enabled a default egress deny policy and an allowlist for a couple of IP ranges.

sanjay_eng: Quick checks: can you run from a pod `dig control.redwood.internal +short` and `curl -v https://control.redwood.internal/health`? Also `kubectl get networkpolicy -A` and `kubectl describe netpol -n redwood` so we can see the rules.

maria_customer: dig returns nothing from the pod. From host node dig works. Pod resolves to nothing. Logs show `lookup control.redwood.internal: no such host`.

liz_sre: Sounds like egress to your cluster DNS (CoreDNS -> VPC resolver) is blocked. If pods can't reach the VPC DNS, they'll fail to resolve control plane and people sometimes curl the control plane IP directly which causes SNI/cert CN mismatch -> TLS handshake error.

alex_support: Repro steps we tried in a test cluster: `kubectl run -it --rm debug --image=appropriate/curl --namespace redwood --command -- sh` then inside pod `dig control.redwood.internal` -> no result. Then `curl -v https://10.0.8.12:443` -> got cert CN mismatch. So two distinct failures: DNS resolution failing, and IP-based access causing SNI mismatch.

maria_customer: Our egress rules only allowed a small CIDR and didn't include the control plane CIDR nor the VPC resolver (10.0.0.2). We assumed 0.0.0.0/0 allow for 443 covered it but Calico netpol was scoped differently.

sanjay_eng: Try adding explicit egress allows for:
- control plane CIDR (e.g. 10.0.8.0/24)
- your VPC DNS resolver (10.0.0.2 or aws resolver IP)
Example snippet (Calico/NetworkPolicy):

`egress:
  - to:
      - ipBlock:
          cidr: 10.0.8.0/24
    ports:
      - port: 443
        protocol: TCP`

maria_customer: Added allow for control plane CIDR and for 10.0.0.2. Ran `kubectl exec debug -- dig control.redwood.internal` -> now returns 10.0.8.12. `curl https://control.redwood.internal/health` -> 200 OK, TLS handshake OK. :white_check_mark:

liz_sre: Great. Root cause: Calico NetworkPolicy default-deny egress blocked DNS queries to the VPC resolver and blocked TLS SNI-preserving resolution path. When pods fell back to IP, SNI mismatch triggered SSL failures.

alex_support: Action items:
- we'll add a KB entry and sample NetworkPolicy to the Redwood Private install docs recommending explicit egress allow for control plane CIDR and VPC DNS resolver.
- file an engineering ticket for the agent to emit a clearer log when control-plane health checks fail due to DNS/egress blocks.

sanjay_eng: I'll open INF-3421 with reproduction steps and suggested policy snippet.

maria_customer: Thanks everyone — policy adjusted and service is healthy again. Appreciate the quick help.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-agent v2.14 started (no network changes).
